title: Recording Audio Tricks
intro: These tricks are about getting a clean, usable, well‑organised take the first time, and not losing a good performance to a technical mistake.

tips.t: Aim your peaks at −12 to −18 dBFS
tips.d: Aim for your loudest peaks to land between −12 and −18 dBFS. In 24-bit, recording hot won't improve the real-world noise performance. It just makes the track harder to mix against others recorded with sensible headroom.

src.label: Sound On Sound — Q. How much headroom should I leave with 24-bit recording?
Sound On Sound — Q. Should I gain-stage to -6dBFS or -18dBFS?

tips.t: Track at the lowest I/O buffer your Mac can handle
tips.d: Set the buffer before tracking, not during. In Logic Pro > Settings > Audio > Devices, choose the lowest I/O Buffer Size your Mac can handle. If you get system overload alerts, step it up one setting. Logic shows the resulting latency under the I/O Buffer Size menu, so judge by that readout, not the sample number.

src.label: Apple — Manage input monitoring latency in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Turn on Low Latency Monitoring mode instead of disabling plug-ins one by one
tips.d: Low Latency Monitoring mode bypasses the latency-inducing plug-ins that push a track past the Limit slider in Logic Pro > Settings > Audio > General (up to 30 ms). It also turns off that track's Aux sends, which kills a headphone reverb fed from a send. It affects only the focused instrument track and tracks with Input Monitoring or Record Enable on.

src.label: Apple — Work with plug-in latencies in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Count-in and pre-roll are either/or — pick the right one
tips.d: In the Recording project settings, the When Beginning buttons make you choose a count-in or a pre-roll. Count-in is set in bars or beats. Pre-roll is a playback time in seconds, up to 60. Use pre-roll when bars mean nothing (free-tempo material, dialogue) and count-in when you want the performer counted in musically.

src.label: Apple — Recording project settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Name the track before you record, always
tips.d: Regions that use the track name as their region name, and their source audio files, follow a default track name like “Audio 3”. That name means nothing to you three months later.

src.label: Apple — Rename tracks in Logic Pro for Mac (from prior audit; not re-retrieved this session)

tips.d: Click the Record Enable button in the track header of each track you want to record to — every armed button blinks red. Option-click is the escape hatch, not the shortcut: Option-clicking a track's Record Enable button makes it the only record-ready track, and Option-clicking a track that is already blinking red clears record-ready status across the whole project. Learn it as "solo the arm" and "disarm everything".

src.label: Apple — Record to multiple audio tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: ⌘. discards the take you just recorded
tips.d: Press ⌘. — Discard Recording and Return to Last Play Position — to stop and throw away the take you just recorded, for when you know instantly it was not the one.

src.label: Apple — Advanced recording commands in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Watch the take list, not the waveform
tips.d: The Take Folder pop-up menu in the upper-left corner of a take folder lists every take you've banked, and you can pick one from it during playback. If the performer is on take 14 and getting worse, that list is your cue to stop and move on.

src.label: Apple — Preview take recordings in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Create and save comps in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Build a dedicated headphone mix on a bus
tips.d: Select every channel strip, choose a bus in a Send slot, and route the aux channel strip Logic creates to the output that feeds the headphone amp. Give the performer more of themselves and more reverb than you would ever put in the mix. Comfort produces better takes than accuracy does.

src.label: Apple — Send a mix to multiple destinations in Logic Pro for Mac (from prior audit; not re-retrieved this session)

tips.t: Use Input Monitoring rather than record enable to rehearse
tips.d: The Input Monitoring (I) button in the track header lets you hear a track that isn't record-enabled, so you can set levels and practise the part before committing. On audio tracks it still involves some latency, depending on your hardware and driver settings.

src.label: Apple — Use input monitoring with tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Turn off Software Monitoring when your interface can monitor
tips.d: Software monitoring always carries some delay. Apple's advice when your interface supports hardware monitoring: turn off Software monitoring in Logic Pro > Settings > Audio > General, or with its control bar button.

tips.t: Give the performer a click they can feel
tips.d: Swap the metronome sound, add a bar accent, or better, program a simple drum loop. A musical reference beats a woodblock every time.
